info.title: ERP API v2
info.description: Provides a common API surface for accessing ECI ERP products. ## ERP Product Support This version of the API is generally supported by: - Deacom - M1 - Macola - JobBOSS² Support for some resources varies, so check the *Supported ERPs* section on each resource to see if it's supported before using it. The API user account used to access the ERP API determines which ERP Product, Customer, and any specific database (Instance) of that ERP that will be accessed. Depending on the product, the actual ERP database could be a cloud hosted ERP or on premises install, therefore, performance of the API may vary dramatically. The [user-info endpoint](#/Account/get_api_v1_user_info) in this API will provide basic information about the user account and company being accessed, such as the companyId and product. It should be noted that the **CompanyID** does not uniquely identify the instance being accessed via the API. ## Authentication Pass an access token in the HTTP Authorization header of each request. For example: ```Authorization: Bearer [token]``` Access tokens are obtained from the Management API. See the Management API OAuth 2.0 Token endpoint documentation for more information. ## Field Selection For resources that support Field Selection, the `fields` parameter can be provided with a comma separated list of fields to return in the result. For example: ```/api/v2/organizations?fields=name,country``` ## Filter Expressions For resources that support filtering, filter expressions can be applied as query string parameters in the format ```field_name[operator]=value``` Note, for simple equality, you can omit the operator and specify fieldname=value. e.g. ```?firstName=Jane``` ### Operators - [eq] Equal to the given value. - [ne] Not Equal to the given value. - [gte] Greater than or equal to the given value. - [lte] Less than or equal to the given value. - [gt] Greater than the given value. - [lt] Less than the given value. - [in] Is in a list of pipe separated values. - [notin] Is not in a list of pipe separated values. ## Sort Expressions For resources that support sorting, the sort expression is specified by adding the ```sort``` query string parameter, with a comma separated list of expressions as its value, each expression having an optional prefix of + or - to indicate ascending or descending order. For example: ``` ?sort=firstname ?sort=lastname,firstname ?sort=-create_date ``` ## Paging Parameters The parameters ```take``` and ```skip``` can be provided separately but can be combined to implement server-side paging of results. See the documentation for take and skip on each resource. For example: ``` ?take=100 ?take=100&skip=200 ``` ## Count Parameter The parameter ```count``` may be provided to change the data retrieval behavior. The value of `0` returns the filtered, expanded, and paginated data in the `data` property of the response. The `count` property always contains the number of records in `data`. This is the default behavior when the `count` parameter is not provided. The value of `1` returns an empty array in the `data` property and the total count of matching source records in the `count` property, applying any requested filters but ignoring any requested paging parameters. The value of `2` returns both the `data` records, paginated if requested, and the `count` value with the total number of records in the source, ignoring pagination. ``` 0 - Data Only 1 - Total Count Only 2 - Data and Total Count ``` ## Expansions Some data sources have relationships that can be expanded. The list of supported expansions is located in the documentation for each resource below. An expansion expression is in the form: ```expand=relationship_name(fields_expression)``` fields_expression is optional. For example, to expand the timecard for a timecard line ```api/v1/view/timecardlines?expand=timecard``` A resulting individual record would look like: ```json { "timecardID": 5, "timecard": { "timecardID": 5, "employeeID": "GROSE", "shiftID": 1, "timecardDate": "2000-11-06T00:00:00", "uniqueID": "389fcb16-8740-467f-9273-9c383f1472c9", "rowVersion": 27569 } } ``` To select only specific fields from an expansion, use an inner fields expression. ```api/v1/view/timecardlines?expand=timecard(fields=uniqueid,employeeID)``` And the resulting record would look like: ```json { "timecardID": 5, "timecard": { "employeeID": "GROSE", "uniqueID": "389fcb16-8740-467f-9273-9c383f1472c9" } } ``` Expansions can also be nested. ```api/v1/view/timecardlines?expand=timecard(expand=employee)``` ## ConvertToUTC The time zone in which Date/Time values are represented varies by ERP and some times data source. Pass the ConvertToUTC parameter with a value of `yes` to indicate you want supported date/time field values converted to UTC. ```api/v1/view/timecardlines?ConvertToUTC=yes``` See resource specific documentation for which fields are supported. ## Common Attributes ### uniqueID The ```uniqueID``` attribute, when present, uniquely identifies a record in the source system. This identifier may not be globally unique. It is only guaranteed to be unique for the same resource and same Company account. In general, the ERPs use the following data types in the uniqueID field: - Macola: GUID - M1: GUID - JobBOSS²: Int32 ### rowVersion The value of the rowVersion attribute is a 64bit signed integer. This value can be used to query for new or modified records in most resources. New and updated records will always receive a value higher than the rowVersion of any other record in the source data. There may be some variations in the implementation of this attribute across ERP products. ## Tracing This API supports [W3C Trace Context](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/). TraceIDs will be generated for each request and returned in each response in a *traceid* header. You should capture this value in any responses and consider logging it as part of any integration being built. When reporting problems with this API, the *traceid* in the response is the single most important piece of information you can provide. ``` traceid: 00-e352fa809e1a5b47ba4d88f8182b36f4-44902b415c593c4f-00 ``` In addition, the traceid value is provided in the body of error responses. ```json { "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.4", "title": "Not Found", "status": 404, "traceId": "00-c2857fd044158e41bf73349e95208f1e-9476acc2107e274d-00" } ``` A caller can also provide their own W3C Trace Context compliant trace id via the ```traceparent``` heeder in a request. ``` traceparent: 00-0af7651916cd43dd8448eb211c80319c-b7ad6b7169203331-01 ``` ## Error Responses Error responses will typically be in in [RFC7807](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7807) "Problem details" format as show below: ### A sample 404 Not Found ```json { "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.5.4", "title": "Not Found", "status": 404, "traceId": "00-c2857fd044158e41bf73349e95208f1e-9476acc2107e274d-00" } ``` ### A sample 500 Internal Server Error ```json { "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-6.6.1", "title": "An error occured while processing your request.", "status": 500, "traceId": "00-fd1c6ec035a01943bec2ffabf2f1d6e2-9601a3cae715e143-00" } ``` ## Response Headers - **traceid:** The W3C Trace Context (see above) - **erp-company-id**: A value identifying the ERP Company where the data in the response originated. - **erp-instance-id**: A value indicating the database instance being accessed. Note this value is presently not immutable, and may change periodically. - **cdc-request-id**: For requests that were executed via a Cognytics Data Connector request, this provides the CDC Request ID ## Management Console Use the Integration Engine Management Console to configure and monitor access to this API. ## Contact Information This API is maintained by the ECI Manufacturing Integration Team.
